newsitem.title: USA: US Spot Products- US Gulf low sulphur jet bid firm.
newsitem.headline: US Spot Products- US Gulf low sulphur jet bid firm.

text.p: Low sulphur jet fuel was bid firm through July on Thursday reflecting a contango futures spread that is providing incentive to store the petroleum product and sell it at the more expensive price it has acquired in the later months.
New York Harbor heating oil was also talked firmer, resisting a lower price posting by Sun Co on Thursday while reformulated gasoline remained weak.
Midcontinent values held their stronger levels following refiner product shipment delays though dealings were quiet.

July heating oil futures on the NYMEX were 0.18 cent a gallon higher at 51.70 cents, putting the spot month at a 0.55 cent contango to August. Contango means the earlier futures contract is less expensive than the later one.
July gasoline was 0.51 cent higher a 57.05 cents a gallon.
U.S. GULF

Low sulphur jet fuel was bid at even to July heating oil through July after being bid below the July contract early in the week, though dealers had not heard of any trades to confirm the firmer level.

"The market is just catching up to where it should be. At this time of year, dealers can take advantage of the carry (contango) and store it to sell it later on," said a U.S. Gulf jet dealer, adding offers were about 0.25 cent above July heat.
Dealers said prompt 55-grade low sulphur jet should usually trade at a 0.40 to 0.50 cent premium to prompt airline quality jet fuel which was bid at 0.50 cent under July heat.
Meanwhile, prompt regular conventional M1 gasoline differentials deteriorated following the scheduling deadline Wednesday on the Colonial Pipeline, traders said.

Prompt M1 was talked near 2.00 cents under the July NYMEX, about 0.50 cent off Wednesday's levels. Prompt barrels had jumped to 1.25 cents under the July NYMEX ahead of the scheduling deadline, but began falling back by late Wednesday, according to traders.
Reformulated gasoline showed some modest weakness, with traders putting prompt barrels at even with the July NYMEX price.
NEW YORK HARBOR
Heating oil differentials in the Harbor strengthened from a Sun Co posting Wednesday that was deemed too soft for the market and had the refiner boosted its posting Thursday.
"There is plenty of supply of heating oil, but Sun's level was still too low," said a Harbor trader.

Sun Co chaned its posting to 0.30 cent under July heat after posting at 0.40 cent under Wednesday. Consequently, prompt heating oil was talked between 0.35 and 0.10 cent under July heat versus 0.75 and 0.50 cent under.
Reformulated gasoline was still talked between even tio 0.,25 cent under NYMEX july gasoline after two barges traded at 0.25 cent under early in the week.

High imports and refinery out have created a sufeit of refimrutaletd gasoline in the Harbor, although dealers noted the Europe to United States arbotrage is now shut which may moderate the next wave of imports.
MIDCONTINENT

Midcontinent market unleaded gasoline differentials held firm in spotty trade on Thursday as the any months were pressured by the delay on the Explorer Pipeline system. Group Three unleaded differentials held steady at 6.00/6.25 cents over July NYMEX, after gaining about a half cent on Wednesday.
The Explorer system has said its 17th cycle June barrels will be delayed until July 1st or 2nd, instead of arriving Tulsa, Oklahoma, on June 22nd.
Any month barrels were up a half cent to 4.00 cents, with the 4.00 cent traded.
Chicago markets were also firm, with prompt about a quarter to half cent higher amid more buyers than sellers. Deals were done at 4.25 cents of the print.
-- New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1620
